title: Mineral hardness (example)
blurb: What hardness is, the ten Mohs reference minerals and quick field tests.
h1: Mineral hardness and the Mohs scale
lede: A small example lecture written only as data files. It shows every feature: steps, questions, vocabulary, flashcards, tables and fill-the-gap facts.
six: **Hardness** is how well a mineral resists being scratched.
The **Mohs scale** ranks 10 reference minerals from **1 (talc)** to **10 (diamond)**.
It is a **ranking**, not equal steps: diamond is far harder than corundum.
A harder mineral scratches a softer one, never the other way round.
Fingernail is about **2.5**, a copper coin about **3.5**, a steel knife or glass about **5.5**.
**Quartz is 7**: it scratches glass and a steel knife.
foot: Example content to demonstrate the data-file format. Not part of any course.

questions.q: Which mineral is the hardest on the Mohs scale?
questions.e: Diamond is 10, the top of the Mohs scale.

questions.q: Which mineral is the softest on the Mohs scale?
What is the Mohs hardness of quartz?
questions.e: Quartz is 7. It is one of the most common minerals.

questions.q: What kind of scale is the Mohs scale?
questions.answer: A ranking: it shows order, not equal differences
questions.e: Mohs is ordinal. The gap between 9 and 10 is much bigger than between 1 and 2.

questions.q: How many reference minerals does the Mohs scale have?

questions.e: A mineral scratches another only if it is harder. Fluorite is 4, calcite is 3.

questions.q: A fingernail (about 2.5) can scratch which mineral?
questions.e: 2.5 is harder than gypsum (2) but softer than calcite (3).

questions.q: Which common object has a hardness of about 5.5?
questions.e: Glass and a steel knife blade are both about 5.5.

questions.q: What is the streak of a mineral?
questions.answer: The colour of its powder on an unglazed porcelain plate
questions.e: Streak is the colour of the powder. It is often more reliable than the colour of the whole mineral.

questions.answer: Breaking along flat planes of weakness
questions.e: Cleavage follows planes in the crystal structure. Breaking in an irregular way is called fracture.

questions.q: Which is harder: corundum or topaz?
questions.e: Corundum is 9, topaz is 8. Ruby and sapphire are corundum.

questions.answer: How the surface of a mineral reflects light
questions.e: Lustre can be metallic, glassy, pearly, dull and so on.

vocab.meaning: How well a mineral resists being scratched.
A ranking of ten reference minerals from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond).
The colour of a mineral's powder, seen when it is rubbed on unglazed porcelain.
How the surface of a mineral reflects light.
The tendency to break along flat planes of weakness.
Breakage that does not follow cleavage planes, for example the curved breaks of quartz.
Mohs hardness 1, the softest mineral on the scale.
Mohs hardness 2; a fingernail can scratch it.
Mohs hardness 9; ruby and sapphire are varieties of it.
Mohs hardness 10, the hardest natural mineral.

facts: Hardness is how well a mineral resists being {scratched|dissolved|heated|weighed}.
On the Mohs scale, {talc|quartz|calcite|topaz} is the softest mineral.
The Mohs scale has {10|5|7|12} reference minerals.
Quartz has a Mohs hardness of {7|5|6|9}.
A fingernail has a hardness of about {2.5|1.5|4.5|5.5}.
Window glass has a hardness of about {5.5|3.5|7|9}.
